reason: The quote is exact: AdminDeployManager.java:656-661 removes the index, calls saveSpawnPoints() and unconditionally returns true, and the identical shape is at :692-697 (removeMobSpawnPoint) and :728-733 (removeVillager), so a write failure cannot reach the caller through the boolean; ArenaAdminService's javadoc at :242/:264/:286 explicitly promises 'false on write failure', which is the contract the GUI relies on at ArenaManageGUI.java:496-497 ('deleted' vs 'delete-failed'). The failure is reachable: saveSpawnPoints() returns false both when the shared arenas.yml gate has latched read-only (AdminDeployManager.java:458-462, YamlFileGate.java:52-62/74-81; latch is set permanently for the process on any later failed load) and when gate.write throws IOException (YamlFileGate.java:88-98), while the in-memory savedSpawnPoints.remove() has already happened before the call. However the impact narrative overstates persistence loss: after a failed gate.write the code still pushes the shortened list to the live GameManager (AdminDeployManager.java:530-534), and every future successful saveSpawnPoints() re-serialises savedSpawnPoints into a fresh disk copy (lines 471-511), so the very next successful deployment edit of that arena re-persists the deletion — 'the deletion is lost on restart' only holds if the server restarts before any later successful save; the read-only latch also emits a console SEVERE/warning (YamlFileGate.java:75-79, 95-97), so a failure signal does exist outside the GUI. The command path is already remediated (HilltopCommandHandler.java:989-991/1060-1062/1142-1144 call reportDeploySaveFailure right after), so the defect is confined to the ArenaManageGUI and SetupWizard deletion clicks, and its real cost is a misleading 'Deleted #n' toast plus a resurrected point after an immediate restart — recoverable by re-deleting, with no crash, corruption or irreversible data loss.
